messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: routing.fallback.loop detected — high rate of fallback redirects between us-east <-> us-west <-> eu. Error spike and elevated latency. Alert level: P1.

maya (oncall): seeing the same in graphs, traffic is oscillating between regions every ~30s. some requests keep following the fallback chain.

sam (sre): initial hypothesis: health-check flapping + policy weight adjustments causing three-way oscillation. possibly the dynamic variant selector is choosing a heavier model in us-east then failing over to us-west which then flips back.

alina (eng-platform): tagging routing policy owners. I can pause the automatic fallback policy if we need to stop the churn quickly. thoughts?

maya (oncall): please pause. customer-facing latency is bad; Support reporting timeouts for some sessions.

priya (support): customers impacted: a handful of enterprise orgs in NA and EU (support tickets 5472, 5473). they're seeing long tail latencies and occasionally 5xx from the model service.

jon (eng-runtime): logs show a mismatch: some requests get routed to model variant `gpt-7b-optimized` which needs large KV cache; other region nodes are returning health=degraded due to KV OOM and then routing flips. failing healthchecks look legitimate.

lucas (prodops): immediate mitigation plan: 1) freeze fallback policy (stop automated weight shifts) 2) constrain model variant selection to `gpt-7b-lowkv` for the affected routes 3) throttle new sessions into the chain. I can apply 1 and 2 now.

alina (eng-platform): executing step 1: `PATCH /policies/fallback` payload `{\n  "auto_adjust": false,\n  "note": "emergency freeze - 1765001234"\n}` — applied.

alina (eng-platform): applying constrained selector: `PATCH /routes/cli/selector` `{\n  "allowed_variants": ["gpt-7b-lowkv"]\n}` — pushed to us-east/us-west/eu.

maya (oncall): I put temporary route rule to prefer region local if latency < 50ms to reduce cross-region handoffs.

sam (sre): after freeze + selector change, fallbacks stopped in the metrics. latency dropping from 1200ms p95 to ~420ms p95 in the last 90s.

priya (support): update for customers, pls. I'll post a note in the affected tickets: "We've temporarily constrained model variants and frozen fallback policy to stop a routing oscillation; we are investigating root cause and will follow up."

jon (eng-runtime): root cause candidate: the health-check sensitivity in eu nodes is too aggressive with our current kernel + quantization profile for `gpt-7b-optimized`. When a few requests hit and KV grows, health transitions to `degraded` -> routes out -> other region gets load -> then recovers -> repeat. We'll need to tune health check hysteresis or the memory accounting.

sam (sre): next steps: create a canary config that increases healthcheck window and reduces false-degrades; also add a circuit-breaker so that once a region health flips N times in M seconds we stop routing to it for T minutes without further oscillation.

alina (eng-platform): logged ticket PLAT-9831 for fallback policy hysteresis and circuit-breaker. assigning to jon and sam.

lucas (prodops): rolling back the `gpt-7b-optimized` variant from selectors globally would be heavier; good call to constrain routes first. we should also bump capacity on us-east for short term in case we see surge.

maya (oncall): handing off to sam for post-incident investigation. I'm going offline for rest of shift, but will stay reachable on phone if needed.

sam (sre): taking lead. I have access to the half-hour of pre-freeze logs and will correlate health transitions with variant assignments. tagging @oncall-next for follow-up.

priya (support): customers updated. ticket notes: "Mitigation applied; expecting normalized latency. We'll send a postmortem with timeline and root cause next business day."

jon (eng-runtime): quick patch idea: change healthcheck to require 2 consecutive fails over 45s instead of 3 over 15s, and add a `recent-fail-count` guard to the smart router. I'll draft a change; won't push to prod without coordination.

alina (eng-platform): can we add a metric/alert for repeated flip counts per region so SRE sees this earlier?

sam (sre): yes, creating an SRE playbook entry and metric: `routing.region.flip_rate` with alert at >3 flips/min.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied (fallback freeze, selector constraint). Severity downgraded to P2 for investigation and postmortem.

maya (oncall): thanks team. please add a summary to #postmortems once we have the timeline.

sam (sre): will do. timeline so far will include: alert->freeze 00:02 -> selector constrain 00:05 -> normalized 00:07 -> handoff 00:10. I'll collect logs and message when postmortem is ready.

lucas (prodops): note for follow-up: run replay with synthetic KV pressure to reproduce. adding runbook step.

priya (support): closing live update. customers acknowledged and waiting on postmortem.

sam (sre): closing thread for live triage, leaving action items: PLAT-9831 (policy hysteresis), RUNTIME-2209 (healthcheck tuning), SRE-301 (flip_rate alert).

maya (oncall): :white_check_mark: all good here, handing off to next oncall.
